newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks extend winning streak at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks extend winning streak at open.

text.p: Australian shares made modest extensions to Friday's record-breaking run at the open on Monday with much of the market treading water ahead of the federal government's 1997/98 budget due late on Tuesday local time.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index added 6.8 points to 2,532.8, supassing the previous record high of 2,528.1 reached on May 9.
Having set up camp in the high ground above the 2,500 level last week, the market made itself comfortable in the rarefied air as traders awaited Tuesday's budget.
"It is still looking good," said a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage. "We just have to wait and see what (Treasurer Peter) Costello delivers."

The leaders were largely marking time with mixed, narrow moves, while at the smaller end colourful West Australia-based gold miner St Barbara topped turnover with a line of 10.35 million shares specialled through Porter Western at a price of A$0.72 per share (US$0.56). St Barbara shares were 2.7 cents higher at 65 cents.
Oil and gas explorers Novus Petroleum and Energy Equity showed strong gains after well-received progress reports from their Singa 1 well in Indonesia.
Novus shares jumped three percent to a record high at A$4.35 while Energy Equity leapt 17 percent to A$1.567, also a record.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about five to two, while about 45 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
